item.title: AI Maps Six Hidden Earth Structures
item.description:
AI Maps Six Hidden Earth Structures

About 1,800 miles beneath your feet, Earth’s mantle meets the liquid outer core. That contact is not a smooth seam. It is a landscape. For decades seismologists have known that the base of the mantle is lumpy, with patches of odd material that scatter passing earthquake waves. Mapping those patches has always been a fight against faint signals and uneven coverage. A new effort from Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers uses a deep-learning system, a mountain of old seismograms, and a lot of human cleanup to argue that the lumps are more connected, and more numerous, than earlier catalogs showed.
